name: Mercury
tagline: The Swift Planet closest to the Sun
summary: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and closest to the Sun. It is only slightly larger than Earth's Moon. From the surface of Mercury, the Sun would appear more than three times as large as it does when viewed from Earth.
interestingFacts: Mercury is the fastest planet, zooming around the Sun at 47 km/s.
Despite being closest to the Sun, Venus is hotter than Mercury.
Mercury has a giant impact basin named Caloris Basin, 1,550 km across.
A day on Mercury (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days.

name: Venus
tagline: Earth's toxic twin shrouded in golden clouds
summary: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and Earth's closest planetary neighbor. It is often called Earth's twin because it's similar in size and structure, but Venus has extreme surface heat and a thick, toxic atmosphere full of carbon dioxide and sulfuric acid.
interestingFacts: Venus spins backward relative to most other planets (retrograde rotation).
One day on Venus is longer than one year on Venus.
Surface atmospheric pressure on Venus is 90 times higher than Earth's.
Venus is the brightest natural object in Earth's night sky after the Moon.

name: Earth
summary: Earth is our home planet, the third planet from the Sun, and the only place inhabited by living things known so far. While Earth is only the fifth largest planet in the solar system, it is the only world with liquid water on its surface.
interestingFacts: 71% of Earth's surface is covered in water.
Earth is protected by a powerful magnetic field generated by its molten iron core.
Atmosphere is composed of 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% other gases.
Earth is the only planet not named after a Greek or Roman deity.

name: Mars
tagline: The Red Planet of dusty deserts and ancient volcanoes
summary: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun—a dusty, cold, desert world with a very thin atmosphere. Mars is also a dynamic planet with seasons, polar ice caps, canyons, extinct volcanoes, and evidence that it was even more active in the past.
interestingFacts: Mars is home to Olympus Mons, the largest volcano in the solar system (21.9 km high).
It has two small irregularly shaped moons: Phobos and Deimos.
The red color is due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.
Valles Marineris on Mars is a canyon system 10 times longer than the Grand Canyon.

name: Jupiter
summary: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined. The giant planet's familiar stripes and swirls are actually cold, windy clouds of ammonia and water, floating in an atmosphere of hydrogen and helium.
interestingFacts: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is an enormous storm bigger than Earth that has raged for centuries.
Jupiter has the shortest day of all solar system planets (under 10 hours).
Its moon Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system, bigger than Mercury.
Jupiter acts as a gravitational shield protecting inner planets from asteroids.

name: Saturn
tagline: The Ringed Jewel of the Solar System
summary: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest planet in our solar system. Adorned with thousands of beautiful ringlets, Saturn is unique among the planets. It is not the only planet to have rings, but none are as spectacular or complex.
interestingFacts: Saturn is so low in density that it would float in a giant bathtub of water.
Its rings are made mostly of ice particles, rocky debris, and dust.
Titan, Saturn's largest moon, has lakes of liquid methane and a dense atmosphere.
Saturn has a mysterious hexagonal jet stream storm at its north pole.

name: Uranus
summary: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, and has the third-largest diameter in our solar system. It was the first planet found with the aid of a telescope, discovered in 1781 by astronomer William Herschel.
interestingFacts: Uranus rotates almost completely on its side with an axial tilt of 97.77°.
It is an ice giant, composed mostly of water, methane, and ammonia ice.
Methane gas in its upper atmosphere gives Uranus its distinctive pale cyan hue.
It reaches the coldest temperatures recorded of any solar system planet (-224°C).

name: Neptune
summary: Dark, cold, and whipped by supersonic winds, ice giant Neptune is the eighth and most distant major planet in our solar system. More than 30 times as far from the Sun as Earth, Neptune is the only planet not visible to the naked eye.
interestingFacts: Neptune has the fastest recorded winds in the solar system, reaching 2,100 km/h.
It was mathematically predicted by Urbain Le Verrier before it was visually observed in 1846.
Neptune's largest moon Triton orbits in reverse (retrograde) and has geysers.
Sunlight on Neptune is 900 times dimmer than on Earth.
